title: Why Some People Sneeze At Sunlight

scenes.say: Some people sneeze when they look at the sun. And it's in their genes.
It's called the photic sneeze reflex.
scenes.heading: IT HAS A NAME

scenes.say: Somewhere between one in ten and one in three people have it.
scenes.heading: HOW COMMON?

scenes.say: Its other name is honestly perfect. The ACHOO syndrome.
scenes.heading: ITS OTHER NAME

scenes.say: Why does it happen? The leading theory: the nerve for your eyes runs close to the nerve that triggers sneezing.
scenes.heading: THE THEORY

scenes.say: Bright light hits your eyes, and the signal spills over.
And it runs in families. If one parent has it, there's about a fifty percent chance you will too.
scenes.heading: THE FAMILY PART

scenes.say: Do you sneeze at the sun?
